```text
44-### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)
45-
46-Line numbers are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f`.
47-
48-- **Where partial entries leave the map today.** `UserAvailabilityService.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` returns early for any entry that fails `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:748`). The predicate is at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:228`. The partial entries go to `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` instead (`date-ranges.ts:248`, called at `getUserAvailability.ts:482`).
49-- **Why the slots vanish.** The partial ranges are appended to the busy times (`getUserAvailability.ts:651-657`) and subtracted from both `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`:659-660`). A whole-day entry is different: it stays in `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked away, and it is removed only from `oooExcludedDateRanges` through `groupedOOO` (`date-ranges.ts:297-300` and `:354-361`). To get away slots, a partial window must follow the same split: subtract it from `oooExcludedDateRanges` only, and keep it in `dateRanges`.
50-- **Booking stays blocked.** `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`), so once the window is removed there, a booking inside it is still rejected. Criterion 2 needs a test for this.
51-- **Slot marking is date-level.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` looks up `datesOutOfOffice[YYYY-MM-DD]` and marks every slot on that date (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:187-221`). It needs a time check for partial entries. `IOutOfOfficeData` (`getUserAvailability.ts:209`) maps a date to one entry, so the type must carry the window (for example optional `start` and `end`, or a list per date). See the open question on two entries in one day.
52-- **The booker assumes away means a whole day.** `AvailableTimes` shows the panel when every slot is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is away, and it hides every away slot (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx:266-293`). A mid-day window has neither its first nor its last slot away, so no panel renders. It must render the panel at the first away slot of each run. `AvailableTimeSlots` decides that a day is away from its first slot only (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`, comment "since OOO is date-level"), which hides the time-format toggle when a window starts the day.
53-- **The redirect.** The "Book with" button is in `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, which calls `router.push` to `/${toUser.username}` with the date. It already works from the slot data, so criterion 4 needs only the data in criterion 1.
```

```text
    ({ user }) => !schedulingType || schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || user?.isFixed
  );

  const fixedDateRanges = mergeOverlappingDateRanges(
    intersect(fixedHosts.map((s) => (!isTeamEvent ? s.dateRanges : s.oooExcludedDateRanges)))
  );
  const dateRangesToIntersect = fixedDateRanges.length ? [fixedDateRanges] : [];
  const roundRobinHosts = userAvailability.filter(({ user }) => user?.isFixed !== true);
  if (roundRobinHosts.length) {
    // Group round robin hosts by their groupId
    const hostsByGroup = roundRobinHosts.reduce(
      (groups, host) => {
        const groupId = host.user?.groupId || DEFAULT_GROUP_ID;
        if (!groups[groupId]) {
          groups[groupId] = [];
        }
        groups[groupId].push(host);
        return groups;
      },
      {} as Record<string, typeof roundRobinHosts>
    );

    // at least one host from each group needs to be available
    Object.values(hostsByGroup).forEach((groupHosts) => {
      if (groupHosts.length > 0) {
        const groupDateRanges = groupHosts.flatMap((s) =>
          !isTeamEvent ? s.dateRanges : s.oooExcludedDateRanges
        );
        dateRangesToIntersect.push(groupDateRanges ?? []);
      }
    });
  }

  const availability = intersect(dateRangesToIntersect);

  const uniqueRanges = uniqueAndSortedDateRanges(availability);
```

```text
// ---------- Linked PRs ----------
const prNumbers = new Set([...issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences.map((p) => p.number), ...extraPrs.map(Number)]);
const linkRe = new RegExp(`(closes|closed|fixes|fixed|resolves|resolved)\\s+#${issueNo}\\b`, "i");
for (const p of gh(["pr", "list", "--state", "all", "--search", `${issueNo} in:body`, "--json", "number,body", "--limit", "30"])) {
  if (linkRe.test(p.body || "")) prNumbers.add(p.number);
}
const prs = [...prNumbers].sort((a, b) => a - b).map((n) => gh(["pr", "view", String(n), "--json",
  "number,title,body,url,state,isDraft,author,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,files,comments,reviews,mergedBy,mergedAt"]));
if (!prs.length) add("PR (D4)", "Linked PR", "FAIL", "no PR links this issue", `Open a PR with \`Closes #${issueNo}\` (\`/pr-draft\`).`);

// ---------- Design (D3): issue body, issue comments, or PR description ----------
const designSources = [{ where: "issue body", text: body }, ...issueComments.map((c) => ({ where: `issue comment by @${c.author.login}`, text: c.body })), ...prs.map((p) => ({ where: `PR #${p.number}`, text: p.body || "" }))];
let design = null;
for (const s of designSources) {
  const at = s.text.search(/alternative/i);
  if (at < 0) continue;
  const after = s.text.slice(at).split(/\n\s*(\*\*)?(rationale|consequences?)\b/i)[0];
  const options = Math.max(listItems(after).length, (after.match(/\boption\s*([0-9]|[A-Z]\b)/gi) || []).length);
  const complete = /rationale/i.test(s.text) && /consequence/i.test(s.text) && /decision/i.test(s.text);
  if (!design || options > design.options) design = { where: s.where, options, complete };
}
add("Design (D3)", "Decision with ≥2 concrete alternatives",
  design ? (design.options >= 2 && design.complete ? "PASS" : "CHECK") : "FAIL",
  design ? `${design.where}: ${design.options} alternative(s) found${design.complete ? "" : "; Decision/Rationale/Consequences not all labelled"}` : "no design decision found",
  "Add Decision / Alternatives (2+) / Rationale / Consequences (`/plan-design`).");
```

```text
// The create handler strips the client's UTC offset before saving, so OutOfOfficeEntry.start and .end hold
// the host's wall-clock time in UTC columns. An entry saved as whole days spans 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999.
export function isWholeDayOutOfOffice({ start, end }: { start: Date; end: Date }): boolean {
  return (
    start.getUTCHours() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMinutes() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCSeconds() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMilliseconds() === 0 &&
    end.getUTCHours() === 23 &&
    end.getUTCMinutes() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCSeconds() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCMilliseconds() === 999
  );
}

// `.tz(timeZone, true)` (keepLocalTime, which processOOO uses for midnight) resolves a wall-clock time that
// falls within a few hours of a DST change against the wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York
// came back as 04:30-05:00. Parsing the wall-clock string in the zone returns 03:30-04:00.
function wallClockToTimeZone(stored: Date, timeZone: string): Dayjs {
  return dayjs.tz(dayjs.utc(stored).format("YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS"), timeZone);
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 15:39:12Z)**_

Your model is mostly right. Two parts need correcting first, because the round-robin problem depends on them:

- **`oooExcludedDateRanges` doesn't mark slots.** Slots are marked "away" by a third structure, the away map (`datesOutOfOffice`). `oooExcludedDateRanges` is the list of times the host can really be booked. It's used for two things: checking a booking, and building slots for team events.
- **The `windows` in the away map are the times the host is away, not the times they're available.** A date with no `windows` means away all day.

So there are three structures per host, all built in `getUserAvailability.ts`:

| Structure | Holds | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `dateRanges` | working hours, minus calendar busy times; OOO **left in** | making the slots for a **single-host** event |
| `oooExcludedDateRanges` | the same, but OOO **taken out** | (a) checking a booking, `ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`; (b) making the slots for a **team** event |
| `datesOutOfOffice` (away map) | date → who's away, why, and (new) `windows` | marking slots `away: true` in `getSlots` |

A slot that is in `dateRanges` and marked away is shown as an away panel and can't be booked.

---

### 1. `packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts`: building the three structures

**What it is:** the service that works out one host's availability.

**What it did before (main, from PR #85).** A partial-day window was turned into a fake busy time and subtracted from **both** lists, the same way a calendar event is:
```ts
// main :656-660
const formattedBusyTimes = [...detailedBusyTimes..., ...partialDayOutOfOfficeRanges];
subtract(dateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);
subtract(oooExcludedDateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);
```

**Why both lists?** I'm inferring this from the code; I didn't find it written down. Back then the away map couldn't hold a time window, only whole dates, so a slot inside the window couldn't be marked away. That left two options:
- remove it only from `oooExcludedDateRanges`: the slot would show as a normal bookable time and then fail when someone booked it, which is worse;
- remove it from both, like a calendar event: the slot disappears cleanly.

PR #85 picked the second option. Removing it from the second list wasn't just to simplify the logic; it's what made the window unbookable. The cost was that nothing on the page explained the gap, which is what issue #104 is about.

**What changed in this PR.** The window is now subtracted **only** from `oooExcludedDateRanges`:
```ts
// PR :704-708
subtract(dateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);                       // window stays → slots get generated
subtract(oooExcludedDateRanges, [...formattedBusyTimes, ...partialDayOutOfOfficeRanges]); // still unbookable
```
It's also added to the away map as a window under its date or dates (`:826-845`). A whole-day entry on the same date wins (`:836`). This copies what whole-day entries already did: keep the time in `dateRanges` and mark it away, take it out of `oooExcludedDateRanges` so it can't be booked. **Confirmed.**

**Assumption:** anything that reads `dateRanges` also looks at the away map. That holds for single-host slots. It doesn't hold everywhere (see file 4).

### 2. `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts`: `buildDateRanges`

**What it is:** turns the schedule into the first versions of `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges`. For every date in the away map, it blanks that whole day in `oooExcludedDateRanges`.

**What changed:**
```ts
// :325-328
.filter(([, dayData]) => !dayData.windows)   // windowed dates are not blanked whole
```
**Why:** windowed dates are now in the map. Without this filter, a 2-hour window would blank the whole day's bookable time. The PR body says the new tests caught exactly that. Only the window itself is subtracted later, in file 1. **Confirmed.**

### 3. `packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts`: marking slots

**What it is:** `getSlots` walks through the ranges it's given in slot-sized steps and looks each slot's date up in the away map.

**What changed:**
```ts
// :14-25
if (!dayData) return undefined;          // date not in map → normal slot
if (!windowsOfDay) return dayData;       // no windows → whole day away (unchanged)
return windowsOfDay.find(w => slotStart < w.end && slotEnd > w.start)?.data;  // overlap → away
```
So "away" is decided here, from the map, not from `oooExcludedDateRanges`. **Confirmed.**

**Assumption:** the map passed in belongs to the person the slots are for. Remember this one; the round-robin problem breaks it.

### 4. Where the round-robin regression comes from: `getAggregatedAvailability.ts` + `trpc/.../slots/util.ts`

Two pieces of existing code meet here.

**(a) Team events build their slots from `oooExcludedDateRanges`, not `dateRanges`:**
```ts
// getAggregatedAvailability.ts:33-36, :65
const isTeamEvent = schedulingType === COLLECTIVE || ROUND_ROBIN || userAvailability.length > 1;
```

For round robin, the hosts' ranges are combined, so a time is offered if **any** host is free. **Confirmed.**

**(b) The slots code passes only the first host's away map to `getSlots`:**

**Confirmed.**

**Example.** A round-robin event with hosts A and B, both working 9–5. A has a 14:00–16:00 entry, and A happens to be first in the list.

| Step | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| A's `oooExcludedDateRanges` | 9–14, 16–17 | 9–14, 16–17 (same) |
| B's `oooExcludedDateRanges` | 9–17 | 9–17 |
| Combined (any host free) | 9–17 → 14:00–16:00 slots exist, through B | same |
| A's away map for that date | **no entry** (partial days never reached the map) | **`{ windows: [14–16] }`** |
| `getSlots` marking 14:00–16:00 | not away → bookable with B ✅ | overlaps A's window → `away: true` ❌ |
| Booking page | shows 14:00, 14:30… | hides them and shows "A is away" |
| API v2 | returns them | drops them (`slots-output.service.ts:49` removes away slots) |

So:
- **The existing shortcut:** `util.ts:1098` uses one host's map for everyone. It was harmless for partial days only because partial days never reached the map.
- **The new change:** putting `windows` into the map (`getUserAvailability.ts:826-845`).
- **What breaks:** round-robin booking pages and API v2 lose times that another host could take. That's also why I marked AC 7 as "Partly".

**Edge cases:**
- It only happens when the host with the entry is first in the list. If A is second, nothing changes, so it can look random.
- **Collective events** (everyone must attend) aren't affected. The hosts' ranges are intersected, so the window is already gone and no slot in it exists to mark.
- **Whole-day entries** already had this problem, so it's pre-existing for them. The PR extends it to partial days.

### 5. Booking page (`AvailableTimes.tsx:273-286`, `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`)
This part just displays whatever `away` flags arrive: each run of away slots becomes one panel. It's correct for the data it gets. In the round-robin case it faithfully shows the wrong flags from file 4.

### In one paragraph
Each host gets two time lists: `dateRanges` (makes the slots for a single-host page; out-of-office time left in) and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (what can really be booked; out-of-office time taken out). The away map decides which generated slots are labelled "away". PR #85 couldn't label part of a day, so it removed the window from both lists and the slots silently vanished. This PR adds `windows` to the away map, which lets it keep the window in `dateRanges` (slots appear), label any overlapping slot away (panel appears), and still remove the window from `oooExcludedDateRanges` (it stays unbookable). The regression comes from older code that labels a whole team's slots using only the first host's map. Before, that map never contained partial-day windows; now it does, so one round-robin host's window hides times the other hosts could take.

2. Why are collective events safe from the regression when round-robin events aren't?
3. What small change at `util.ts:1098` could fix the round-robin case, and what would it cost for whole-day entries?

That's why collective is safe.
- **Round robin** (any one host) is effectively a **union** (`:65`, every host's ranges for a group go into one list). 14:00–16:00 survives through host B, so the slots exist, and host[0]'s map then marks them away.

- **Not this PR's fault:** whole-day entries hiding round-robin slots.
- **This PR's regression:** the same thing for partial-day entries. On `main` those slots are bookable through host B; with this PR they're hidden. That's a small, concrete point to raise with the author.

| Option | Change | Cost / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A. Don't mark team slots | Pass `datesOutOfOffice: undefined` to `getSlots` for team events (`util.ts:1098`) | Simplest. When every host is away, the day just looks empty. |
| B. Mark away only when all hosts are away | Merge the hosts' maps: a slot is away only if it's away in every relevant host's map | Keeps the panel when the whole team is out. _**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 16:11:24Z)**_

Your recap is mostly right. There are four real misunderstandings, plus a few things worth adding.

### What to correct

**1. The two lists hold time ranges, not slots.** `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` are lists of intervals like "Tue 09:00–14:00, Tue 16:00–17:00". Slots (09:00, 09:30, …) are cut from those intervals later, in `getSlots` (`slots.ts`). It matters in two places:
- The booking check doesn't look for a matching slot. It asks whether the booking's start-to-end time fits inside one of the `oooExcludedDateRanges` intervals (`hasDateRangeForBooking`, `ensureAvailableUsers.ts:237`). That's why a 13:45–14:15 booking is rejected without any slot logic.
- "Partial overlap" with a slot is handled in two separate places: by the interval check above for booking, and by the window-overlap test in `slots.ts:14-25` for display.

**2. A full day is "no `windows` field", not "an empty window".**
- When `windows` is present, it always has at least one entry (`getUserAvailability.ts:836-843`). Full day means the field is missing.
- Each map entry is per **date**, not per event. It holds `fromUser`, `toUser` (the redirect), `reason`, `emoji` and `notes`.

**3. Away slots are generated but never shown as times.** This applies to whole days before the PR and to partial days now. The booking page hides every away slot and shows the away panel in its place (`AvailableTimes.tsx:266-286`). So:
- **Whole day:** the attendee sees one panel, no times.
- **Partial day:** times, then a panel, then times.
- Booking is blocked by `oooExcludedDateRanges`, not by hiding. That's why hiding alone is safe: a hand-typed URL still fails the check.

**4. Why have both `oooExcludedDateRanges` and the away map?** Your guess about partial overlap isn't the reason. You're right that one could be derived from the other: `oooExcludedDateRanges` is essentially `dateRanges` minus the away map's times. They're kept separate because they serve different consumers and carry different information:

| | Away map | `oooExcludedDateRanges` |
|---|---|---|
| Answers | "Is this date or time away, and **who / why / redirect to whom**?" | "Is this interval **bookable**?" |
| Shape | per-date labels (+ windows) | plain time intervals, which can't carry a reason or redirect |
| Used by | `getSlots` marking (display) | the booking check, and building **team** slots |

The reason, emoji and redirect can't live in a list of intervals. And the booking check and team aggregation want precomputed intervals they can test quickly, without re-deriving OOO each time. **Confirmed** for the consumers. The motivation is my inference; I didn't find it written down.

### What you missed

- **Single-host and team slots come from different lists.** Single-host slots come from `dateRanges`; team slots come from `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:33-36, :65`). That's why a team page normally has no OOO slots to mark at all, and why round robin only breaks when host B's free time refills the window and host[0]'s map then marks it.
- **The round-robin bug depends on list order.** It only happens when the host with the entry is first. The whole-day version is pre-existing; the partial-day version is new in this PR.
- **How partial days were removed before.** On `main`, a partial-day window was treated as a calendar busy time and subtracted from both lists (`main :656-660`). That's why it disappeared silently, like a meeting would.
- **The `buildDateRanges` filter** (`date-ranges.ts:327`). Without it, a date that has windows would be blanked for the whole day in `oooExcludedDateRanges`.
- **Which entry wins on the same date:**
  - A whole-day entry beats a window (`getUserAvailability.ts:836`).
  - A holiday replaces windows but not a whole-day entry (`:538`).
  - Two windows on one day give two panels.
- **The overlap rule.** Any overlap marks a slot away, including a slot that straddles the leave time. This matches the booking check, so no slot looks bookable and then fails. This was an open question in issue #104.
- **Date keys and time zones.** Windows are stored under the host's local dates. A window past midnight is listed under both dates. The midnight edge case in my review comes from this.
- **Other readers of `away`:**
  - The date picker treats a day as away only if **every** slot is away (`DatePicker.tsx`). That's why a window covering the whole working day looks like a full day (AC 5).
  - The time-format toggle check moved from "first slot away" to "every slot away" (`AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`).
  - API v2 drops away slots entirely (`slots-output.service.ts:49`).

### Your recap, corrected
> `dateRanges` = when the host works, minus meetings, **with OOO left in**. `oooExcludedDateRanges` = the same **with OOO taken out**; it's what bookings are checked against and what team slots come from. The away map = per-date labels (who, why, redirect), and now `windows` for part-day absences; no `windows` means the whole day. Single-host slots are cut from `dateRanges` and marked away where they overlap the map, then the page hides them behind one panel per run. Before this PR, partial days were subtracted from both lists like meetings, so they vanished silently. Round robin breaks because team slots are labelled with only the first host's map, which now contains partial windows. Collective is safe because intersecting the hosts' ranges already removes the window.

## Round-robin test walkthrough

**What we're testing:** a round-robin page should show a time if **any** host is free. The suspected bug is that the page marks slots "away" using **only the first host's** out-of-office data (`trpc/.../slots/util.ts:1098`). So if the first host has a 2:00–4:00pm window, 2:00–4:00 turns into an away panel even though four other hosts are free. A window on any other host should change nothing.

**Seeded setup** (`scripts/seed.ts:1057-1105`):
- Event: **Seeded Team → `round-robin-seeded-team-event`**, 15 minutes, round robin.
- Booking page: `http://localhost:3000/team/seeded-team/round-robin-seeded-team-event`.
- Hosts, with password = username: `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]` (emails `<username>@example.com`).
- The seed attaches them as event users. I haven't traced which one the slots code treats as "first" (`qualifiedHostsService`, **Unverified**). The steps below avoid needing to know by trying hosts one at a time.

### Steps
1. **Baseline.** Pick a weekday 1–2 weeks out, so seeded bookings and minimum notice don't get in the way. Open the booking page on that date while logged out (or in a private window). Note the times around 2:00–4:00pm.
   - **Expected:** a continuous list of 15-minute slots through the afternoon.
   - Also note the page's time zone. The window you create below is in the **host's** zone. If that differs from yours, the gap will appear at a shifted time.

The team booking page doesn't exist in this fork, so you didn't do anything wrong. The "Cal.diy" refactor (`ab21c7f805`) removed Enterprise features, including the team booking pages: there's no `team/[slug]` route under `apps/web/app` any more. So the "preview" sends you to a user's personal page, and `[REDACTED:generic-password]` has no personal events.

The seeded round-robin event does still exist in your database. I checked with a read-only query:
- `round-robin-seeded-team-event`, id **20**, team `seeded-team`.
- 5 hosts, all in Europe/London: `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`, `[REDACTED:generic-password]`.

## What this means for finding 1
The round-robin regression **can't be reached from the web booking page in this fork**. The only paths to it are:
- the public tRPC slots endpoint (`slots.getSchedule`, a `publicProcedure`, `_router.tsx:18`), called directly with `eventTypeId: 20`;
- API v2 slot requests for a team event, if your deployment runs API v2.

So it's still a real code-level change, but much lower severity than I wrote. It's a **risk/nit** rather than a user-facing bug.

_**User (2026-10-29 20:45:08Z)**_

Can you explain this line? "a slot that starts before midnight and runs into a window starting after midnight is not marked away (rare; needs working hours across midnight)"

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:45:26Z)**_

It means a slot can look bookable on the booking page but then fail when someone tries to book it. It only happens when the slot crosses midnight into an out-of-office window that starts on the next date.

### How the lookup works
- **Slots are looked up by their start date.** For each slot, `slots.ts:220-227` takes the date the slot **starts** on (in the host's time zone) and checks the away map **for that date only**.
- **Windows are stored under the dates they touch.** `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows` (`date-ranges.ts:256-277`) lists a window under every date from its start date to its end date. A window from 00:00 to 01:00 on Wednesday is listed only under **Wednesday**.

### Example
The host works a night shift, 20:00–02:00. They add an out-of-office window on **Wed 00:00–01:00**. The event is 30 minutes, with a slot every 15 minutes.

| Slot | Start date (lookup key) | Overlaps the window? | Marked away? | Bookable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tue 23:30–00:00 | Tue | no (ends exactly at 00:00) | no | yes ✅ |
| **Tue 23:45–00:15** | **Tue** | **yes, 00:00–00:15** | **no**: Tue has no windows | **no**: rejected |
| Wed 00:00–00:30 | Wed | yes | yes | no ✅ |

The 23:45 slot is the problem:
- **Display:** the lookup checks Tuesday's entry, which has nothing for this window, so the slot shows as a normal, bookable time.
- **Booking:** the booking check uses `oooExcludedDateRanges`, which has 00:00–01:00 removed. 23:45–00:15 doesn't fit, so `ensureAvailableUsers` rejects it with the "no available users" error.

This is the "looks bookable, then fails" case the PR's any-overlap rule was meant to prevent. Every other overlapping slot is handled, because the window is listed under its own start date and slots starting that day find it.

### Why it's rare
All three of these must be true:
1. **Working hours cross midnight** in the host's time zone. Otherwise no slot exists at 23:45 to cross into the next day.
2. **The window starts at or just after midnight**, on the date after the slot starts.
3. **The slot actually crosses midnight.** With 30-minute events every 30 minutes, the last slot is 23:30–00:00 and only touches midnight. That's no overlap, because the check is strict (`slotEnd > windowStart`, `slots.ts:24`). You need offset slots, like 15-minute steps or a 45-minute event.

### Status and fix
- **Confirmed in code:** I traced the lookup and the date listing. Nobody has run this case.
- **Possible fix:** also list each window under the day before its start date, or check both the slot's start date and its end date. Either is a small change.
- **Severity:** it's a nit because the conditions are so narrow. If the author doesn't fix it, a one-line Tech Debt note would cover it.

Before you set it up: while checking how to reproduce this, I found the slot I described may never exist in the real app. Your test can settle that either way.

### Why it might be impossible
- **Midnight becomes a hard edge.** A schedule that ends at 11:59pm is stretched to exactly midnight (`date-ranges.ts:81-82`). Your 11/9 hours therefore end at 11/10 00:00, and your 11/10 hours start at 00:00. That gives two separate ranges that just touch.
- **Touching ranges aren't joined.** The merge step only joins ranges that truly overlap (`end > nextStart`, strict, in `mergeOverlappingDateRanges.ts:31-35`).
- **A slot must fit inside one range** (`slots.ts:209`). So a 23:45–00:15 slot couldn't be created at all.

The unit test that has a range crossing midnight (`slots.test.ts:843`) builds that range by hand, so it doesn't show the app can produce one. This is my reading of the code and is **Unverified**; your test will show whether it holds.

### Setup (as `pro`, on the PR branch)
1. **Schedule:** confirm 11/9 runs until **11:59pm** and 11/10 starts at **12:00am**, in pro's time zone (Europe/London). The window below is in that zone too.
2. **Make a slot that would cross midnight.** Event Types → `30min` → set the duration to **45 minutes**. With no custom slot interval, slots step by the event length, so evening slots fall at …, 22:15, **23:00 (ends 23:45)**, and then **23:45–00:30**, which would cross midnight. Note the original duration so you can set it back.
3. **Out of office:** add **Tue 11/10, 12:00am–1:00am**, with "All day" off.
4. **Check the page:** open `/pro/30min` on **Mon 11/9** and set the booking page's time zone to **Europe/London** so the times match. Look at the last evening slots.

| 11:45pm hidden or replaced by an away panel | The slot exists and is handled correctly, so my original trace was wrong. Also drop the nit. |

As a control, the 00:00 and 00:45 slots on 11/10 should show up as an away panel. That's the window itself, and it works either way.

```text
## Observed Behavior (OB)
The 11:45pm slot on 11/10 (ending 12:30am on 11/11) is shown as a normal bookable time, although it overlaps an out-of-office window that starts at 12:00am on 11/11. Booking it fails with "Could not book the meeting. No available users found. Could you try another time slot?"

## Expected Behavior (EB)
The slot is marked away, like every other slot that overlaps the window (issue #104, acceptance criterion 1), so it is hidden behind the away panel and never offered.

## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)
1. Seed the database (`yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed`), start the app (`yarn dev`) on the branch with PR #110, and log in as `pro` / `pro` (Europe/London).
2. Availability: set pro's schedule so that 11/10 runs until 11:59pm and 11/11 starts at 12:00am.
3. Event Types → `30min`: set the duration to 45 minutes, so evening slots fall at …, 11:00pm and 11:45pm.
4. Settings → Out of office → Add: 11/11, "All day" off, 12:00am to 9:00am.
5. Open `http://localhost:3000/pro/30min`, choose 11/10, and set the page's time zone to Europe/London.
6. The 11:45pm slot is listed as a normal time. Select it and book.
7. The booking fails with "No available users found".

## Additional Information
**Possible fixes:**
1. In `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows` (`date-ranges.ts:256-277`), also list each window under the date before its start date, so a slot that starts the evening before finds it.
2. In `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` (`slots.ts:220-227`), look up both the slot's start date and its end date, and check the windows of both.

Option 2 keeps the map as it is. Option 1 changes the map's data, which other readers might see. Either needs a unit test with a slot that crosses midnight into a window.

Found in the review of PR #110. Related: issue #104.
```
